geometry_edits.rationale: Open the courtyard toward the site access side so the public threshold is legible at the ground edge.
Increase void generosity slightly to reinforce usable public space while preserving the compact bar mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the courtyard opening to the verified access side so the public threshold becomes legible toward the road frontage.
Slightly enlarge the carved void to strengthen publicness without breaking the dominant bar gesture.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass in all four views, with a readable dominant bar and a centered courtyard/slot that gives the object an actual spatial rule rather than random fragmentation. It responds reasonably to the parcel and does not merely fill the bounding box. The blue frontage edge is not sealed: the top/front views show a legible open ground condition and entry-side carve aligned to the access side in spirit, though the relationship is modest rather than emphatic. Programmatically, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living / mixed-use because it preserves an active ground threshold and a contained public void, with calm upper massing above. The section is not especially expressive, but it is not contradictory to the brief. References support the courtyard-plus-street-edge logic; the tower reference is only partially transferable as hierarchy evidence.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact massing with a legible inner court and street-facing entry moment; the building reads as one coherent body with carved publicness.
Garden-like void and soft enclosure can support neighborhood living if the street edge stays active rather than fully retreating.
Simple low mass with a strong interior threshold suggests how a small program can gain spatial identity through one controlled cut.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Visually more corporate/tall-building than neighborhood living; use only the ground-threshold and stacked-hierarchy principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A mixed ground-and-upper hierarchy can be useful, but the tower-like scale is only a loose analogue here.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Different building type and public-bridge logic; do not copy the form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A linear span or bridge condition can inspire continuity across a void, but the typology is counterfactual to the requested neighborhood mass.

warnings: The access response is somewhat muted; a stronger, more explicit public threshold toward the blue edge would improve program alignment.
The void is useful but not yet deeply articulated as a true public court or terrace.
Upper massing is calm but close to generic extrusion; a slight section profiling could strengthen neighborhood character without changing typology.
